adr03.Title: ADR-03 Enforce approval, safe limits and bounded offline execution for irrigation
adr03.Context: Reliability/Safety and Availability are driving QAs. ASR5 forbids anomalous readings triggering flooding; ASR12 requires controllers to keep the last approved schedule for 48 hours offline; C3 requires 72-hour edge operation. Faulty sensors, invalid requests or outdated schedules could waste water or damage crops. Alternatives: cloud-only control stops watering during rural outages; unrestricted local autonomy continues unsafe or outdated schedules indefinitely; executing requests immediately removes human oversight. A disconnected controller cannot receive cloud cancellations, so offline safety must be enforced locally.
adr03.Decision: Irrigation requests start PENDING and run only after owner approval. Validate units and configurable safe bounds at creation, approval and controller execution; defaults are 1-240 minutes and 0.5-50 mm per request. Only accepted, non-quarantined readings may inform schedules. Approved schedules carry an expiry and a 48-hour offline lease; controllers run them locally during outages and honour local overrides. When the lease lapses without cloud contact, controllers stop automatic watering and revert to manual control. The prototype implements PENDING creation, pending-only replacement and safe-limit validation.
adr03.Consequences: Watering continues through common outages, while invalid requests and faulty readings cannot trigger unbounded irrigation. Approval delays watering. Cloud cancellations cannot reach disconnected controllers until reconnection; expiry and local overrides bound that risk. Safe-state shutdown may under-water during long outages. Per-paddock limits need configuration and agronomic validation.
adr03.Compliance: Test out-of-limit and non-pending requests return 422 and 409. Simulate 48-hour disconnection; confirm local execution, expiry shutdown and manual override. Audit that unapproved schedules never reach controllers.

adr07.Title: ADR-07 Maintain an event-fed farm access projection inside Irrigation and Alerts
adr07.Context: Irrigation and Alerts must confirm farm existence and caller access on every request, but Farm Management owns farms and grants in its own store (ADR-01). ASR19 requires revocation within one minute; ASR26 forbids cross-farm leakage. Alternatives: a shared farm database couples schemas and releases and breaks data ownership; a synchronous call per request adds latency and makes irrigation unavailable whenever Farm Management fails; long-lived response caches risk acting on revoked access. A local copy is safe only if its staleness is bounded and detectable.
adr07.Decision: Farm Management records farm and grant changes in an outbox and publishes versioned, per-farm-ordered events through the Event Broker. Irrigation and Alerts applies them to its own read-only projection: duplicate event IDs are ignored, older versions are discarded, and version gaps trigger resynchronisation from a snapshot. Source heartbeats advance a freshness watermark. New protected mutations return 503 when the watermark is older than 60 seconds or resynchronisation is pending. The prototype seeds the projection from fixture events and implements the deduplication, ordering, gap and freshness rules.
adr07.Consequences: Irrigation keeps working through brief Farm Management outages without shared tables or per-request coupling. Eventual consistency means mutations may be refused during broker delays, reducing availability. The outbox, heartbeats, snapshots and replay add operational complexity. One-minute revocation depends on measured broker latency and remains unvalidated in production.
adr07.Compliance: Automated tests cover revoked grants, duplicate, out-of-order and gap events, and stale watermarks. Production monitoring alerts when projection lag exceeds 30 seconds.

runtime_explanation: Worker creates and edits a validated PENDING request; planned owner approval sends a time-limited schedule to the field controller.
